idea-plugin.name: FitDeveloper
idea-plugin.description:
FitDeveloper — the crunch meter for your IDE with walk-to-unlock breaks.

While the engine is enabled it fills the crunch meter for you and shows a live break countdown (continuous countdown by default — analysis, reading and thinking count as work too; or the classic only-while-typing mode). When the meter reaches 100% a break starts automatically: the QR screen opens and the IDE pauses typing until you have walked the target step count — your phone counts real steps via the DeviceMotion pedometer and syncs live through the plugin's built-in relay server. Finishing the walk unlocks the IDE ("Crunch Break Verified!"). A break always releases itself: after 15 minutes with no walker, or 5 minutes if the walker goes silent. Disable the engine in Settings | Tools | FitDeveloper and nothing is watched, nothing fires, nothing is ever blocked — the master switch, no uninstall needed.

New in 3.2.0 — the whole project now ships under the FitDeveloper name only: repository folders, build and launch scripts, the browser dashboard, the phone walker pages and the standalone variant were all renamed from the old prototype name — same features, one consistent product name.

New in 3.1.0 — sharpened break flow after real-world testing: the QR code now appears in the tool window only when the countdown actually finishes and the break opens (during the countdown the panel stays a pure status display), the idle "waiting room" QR and its confusing phone page were removed, and every decorative symbol was dropped from the walker page so nothing renders as stray characters on phones. The sync indicator stays hidden until the first live sync.

New in 3.0.0 — a cleaner, resizable UI with the QR in the IDE: the tool window is now a status panel (the engine switch, timer mode and minutes live only in Settings — nothing is duplicated), texts and buttons reflow when the widget is resized, and a live QR for the phone walker sits right in the panel (pure Java, works in every IDE — no browser needed). Scanning it joins the open walk directly (shown only while a break is open — refined in 3.1.0). The default countdown is now the research-backed 30 minutes — a ~5-minute walk for every 30 minutes of sitting (Columbia University, 2023; Harvard Health); existing 1.5-min values from older versions migrate to it once, automatically.

New in 2.9.0 — the browser dashboard is fully productized: the manual "Trigger Break Now" button and the demo-walker simulation were removed (breaks now come from the IDE engine alone), the leftover local activity analysis row is gone, and all dashboard texts/badges were updated to the current product behavior.

New in 2.8.0 — the countdown length is now configured in minutes (fractional, 0.5–120) instead of seconds, and the tool window's big countdown renders as minutes:seconds. Fully automatic walk-to-unlock since 2.7.0; two timer modes since 2.6.0.

This is the IDE plugin variant of FitDeveloper — it runs in both IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio (any 2024.2+ based IDE). The standalone variant (runs in a normal browser with a Node server) lives in the without-plugin folder of the same repository.
